# gohatch

> gohatch is a project scaffolding tool for Go, inspired by gonew. It clones templates and rewrites module paths, with support for variable substitution, interactive prompting, hooks, and more.

## Usage

```
gohatch [options] <source> <module> [directory]
```

- `source`: Template source — GitHub shorthand (`user/repo`), full URL (`github.com/user/repo`), or local path (`./template`). Append `@version` for a specific tag, branch, or commit.
- `module`: New Go module path (e.g., `github.com/me/myapp`).
- `directory`: Output directory (optional, defaults to last element of module path).

## Key Features

- [Home](https://gohatch.someonewho.codes/): Installation and quick start
- [Usage](https://gohatch.someonewho.codes/usage/): Full CLI reference with all 11 flags
- [Templates](https://gohatch.someonewho.codes/templates/): Variable syntax, prompting, path renaming, binary detection
- [Creating Templates](https://gohatch.someonewho.codes/creating-templates/): `.gohatch.toml` config, hooks, best practices

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-e, --extension` | Additional file extensions/names for replacement |
| `-v, --var` | Set template variable (`--var Key=Value`) |
| `--dry-run` | Preview without changes |
| `-f, --force` | Skip go.mod validation |
| `--no-git-init` | Skip git init |
| `--keep-config` | Keep .gohatch.toml in output |
| `--verbose` | Detailed progress output |
| `--strict` | Treat unset variables as errors |
| `--no-prompt` | Disable interactive prompting |
| `--no-hooks` | Skip post-generation hooks |

## Template Variables

- Syntax: `__VarName__` (in file contents and path names)
- Default variables: `ProjectName` (directory name), `GitUser` (from module path)
- Set with `--var Key=Value`
- Interactive prompting for unset variables (path vars required, content vars optional)
- `--strict` mode turns unset content variables into errors

## Template Configuration (.gohatch.toml)

```toml
version = 1
extensions = ["toml", "yaml", "justfile"]

[[hooks]]
name = "tidy modules"
command = "go mod tidy"
```

Hooks run after scaffolding with user confirmation. They support variable substitution and have a 5-minute timeout.
